variants.title: Solar cell: I-V curve and fill factor under the lamp at full brightness
variants.unknown: the fill factor at the highest irradiance
variants.note: The light-generated current is proportional to the irradiance on the cell, so moving the lamp is the way the illumination is changed in this experiment.

source.title: M. A. Green, Solar Cells: Operating Principles, Technology and System Applications (photocurrent proportional to irradiance; single-diode model; fill factor)

variants.title: Solar cell: I-V curve and fill factor at half the irradiance
variants.sample: Crystalline silicon cell, lamp at middle distance
variants.unknown: the fill factor at half the irradiance
variants.note: Halving the photocurrent barely moves the open-circuit voltage, because V_oc grows only as the logarithm of the current.

source.title: M. A. Green, Solar Cells: Operating Principles, Technology and System Applications (V_oc logarithmic in photocurrent)

variants.title: Solar cell: I-V curve and fill factor at low irradiance
variants.sample: Crystalline silicon cell, lamp far away
variants.unknown: the fill factor at low irradiance
variants.note: At low light the shunt resistance at the cell's edges takes a larger share of the photocurrent, so the fill factor falls.

source.title: M. A. Green, Solar Cells: Operating Principles, Technology and System Applications (shunt resistance dominates at low irradiance)
